messages.subject: Issues recreating the NMDR model in Stan w/code attached. Would love some pointers to get running.
parts:
I'm a bit new to Stan and I know this is asking a lot, but I would love some pointers on recreating a paper I wrote (http://icml.cc/2012/papers/771.pdf) in Stan so that I can get some best practices (i.e better ways of optimizing the code) and what not to do ever. I'm hoping to create a bunch of models this way, but it would really help me get to a running start to get some feedback. I am running into issues where the final generative portion of the model for my edges are being parameterized by NaNs. The compilation works, but something is off I think in the way I'm creating the stick-breaking conversions. Here is the matlab code for the stick breaking process that works:
   
   K= 10;
   v = randn(K-1,1);

   phi1 = -log(1 + exp(-v));

   phi2 = -log(1 + exp(v));

   logpi(1:K-1) = phi1;

   logpi(2:K) = logpi(2:K) + cumsum(phi2,1);

   pi = exp(logpi);


Here is the Stan code that I was trying to write up for the NMDR model that compiles correctly.:

data {
int<lower=1> K; // number of communities
int<lower=2> N; // number of vertices
int<lower=1> E; // number of edges
int<lower=0, upper=1> Y[E]; // unweighted binary edges
int S[E]; // Row Indices
int R[E]; // Column Indices
int<lower=0> F; // number of features
matrix[N,F] phiF; // Metadata Values
}

parameters {
real<lower=0, upper=10> af;
real<lower=0, upper=10> bf;
real<lower=0, upper=10> av;
real<lower=0, upper=10> bv;
real<lower=0, upper=10> as;
real<lower=0, upper=10> bs;

real<lower=0> lambdaS; // precision prior for metadata mean
vector[F] muEta; // means for metadata weights
vector<lower=0>[F] lambdaF; // precision for metadata weights
matrix[F,K-1] eta; // metadata weights

vector<lower=0>[K-1] lambdaV; // precision for stick-breaking
matrix[N, K-1] v; // continuous stick breaking weights

real<lower=0, upper=1> wa;
real<lower=0, upper=1> wb;
matrix<lower=0, upper=1>[K,K] W; // block connectivity
}


transformed parameters{
row_vector[K-1] phi1;
row_vector[K-1] phi2;
row_vector[K-1] phi3;
matrix[N,K] logpi;
matrix[N,K] pi;

// Create Stick Breaking weights Pi
for (n in 1:N) {
phi1 <- -log(1 + exp(-v[n,:]));
phi2 <- -log(1 + exp(v[n,:]));
logpi[n, 1:K-1] <- phi1;
phi3 <- logpi[n, 2:K] + cumulative_sum(phi2);
logpi[n, 2:K] <- phi3;
pi[n,:] <- exp(logpi[n,:]);
}
}


model {
// Generate metadata priors
lambdaS ~ gamma(as, bs); // recommended by Chung et. al 2013

for (f in 1:F){
muEta[f] ~ normal(0, 1/lambdaS);
lambdaF[f] ~ gamma(af, bf);
}

for (f in 1:F)
for (k in 1:K-1)
eta[f,k] ~ normal(muEta[f], 1/lambdaF[f]);

// Generate continuous stick breaking weights
for (k in 1:K-1)
lambdaV[k] ~ gamma(av, bv);

for (n in 1:N)
for(k in 1:K-1)
v[n,k] ~ normal( phiF[n,:] * eta[:,k], 1/lambdaV[k]);

for (kk in 1:K)
for (ll in 1:K)
W[kk,ll] ~ beta(wa, wb);

for (e in 1:E)
Y[e] ~ bernoulli( pi[S[e],:] * W * pi[R[e],:]' );
}


-------------------------------------------------------
Also I've been able to recreate the MMSB model using Stan with this code which I've attached after this problematic code I'm trying to implement. 

****** Working MMSB Stan Code *********
data {
int<lower=1> K; // number of communities
int<lower=2> N; // number of vertices
int<lower=1> E; // number of edges
vector<lower=0, upper=1>[K] alpha; // Dirichlet prior over mixed memberships
real<lower=0, upper=1> wa; // hyper parameter over stochastic blocks - # heads
real<lower=0, upper=1> wb; // hyper parameter over stochastic blocks - # tails
int<lower=0, upper=1> Y[E]; // unweighted binary edges
int S[E]; // Row Indices
int R[E]; // Column Indices

}

parameters {
simplex[K] pi[N]; // membership probability per vertex
matrix<lower=0, upper=1>[K,K] W; // block connectivity
}

model {
for (v in 1:N)
pi[v] ~ dirichlet(alpha);

for (kk in 1:K)
for (ll in 1:K)
W[kk,ll] ~ beta(wa, wb);

for (e in 1:E)
Y[e] ~ bernoulli( (pi[S[e]])' * W * pi[R[e]] );
}

The simplex variable type implements the standard stick-breaking
construction, so unless you’re doing something non-standard you
should be able to dramatically simplify your model by using simplices
in the parameters block.  Of course you’ll still have to deal with the
strong degeneracies of these kinds of models.  See the LDA section
in the manual for more information.

****** Working MMSB Stan Code *********
data {
int<lower=1> K; // number of communities
int<lower=2> N; // number of vertices
int<lower=1> E; // number of edges
vector<lower=0, upper=1>[K] alpha; // Dirichlet prior over mixed memberships
real<lower=0, upper=1> wa; // hyper parameter over stochastic blocks - # heads
real<lower=0, upper=1> wb; // hyper parameter over stochastic blocks - # tails
int<lower=0, upper=1> Y[E]; // unweighted binary edges
int S[E]; // Row Indices
int R[E]; // Column Indices

}

parameters {
simplex[K] pi[N]; // membership probability per vertex
matrix<lower=0, upper=1>[K,K] W; // block connectivity
}

model {
for (v in 1:N)
pi[v] ~ dirichlet(alpha);

for (kk in 1:K)
for (ll in 1:K)
W[kk,ll] ~ beta(wa, wb);

for (e in 1:E)
Y[e] ~ bernoulli( (pi[S[e]])' * W * pi[R[e]] );
}
